# Architecture

`ms-go-student` is the source of truth for learner profile, ordinary Course attempts and reviews, progression, raw objective evidence, and the current mastery projection. V2 practice catalog and execution are owned by `ms-go-practice-task-orchestrator`. Student retains old practice rows as read-only history and accepts passed v2 Practice evidence through a strict internal contract.

## Boundaries

- `internal/domain` defines statuses, student entities, ports, NATS subjects, and runtime snapshots.
- `internal/usecase/answer` owns attempt lifecycle, final validation, reviews, assessment scoring, results, and course progression.
- `internal/usecase/student` owns learner state, evidence/mastery, legacy practice read compatibility, portfolio projection, and position use cases.
- `internal/transport` owns inbound chi HTTP and NATS command delivery. HTTP routes are separated into `api/v1`, `admin/v1`, and `private` contours.
- `internal/infrastructure` implements PostgreSQL repositories, outbound NATS publishing, downstream HTTP clients, legacy validators, and starter builders.
- `cmd/ms-student-service/main.go` connects concrete adapters and requires PostgreSQL and NATS during startup.

## Ownership

This repository owns:

- `student_task_answer`, automatic/manual review history, and selected assessment variants;
- official attempt status and final-validation outcome;
- `student_position` selections;
- one declared `student_onboarding` profile per student plus a transitional resumable `student_onboarding_draft`; finalize atomically promotes complete answers into the existing profile and clears draft answers, so the draft never becomes a second final profile;
- several simultaneous Student-owned Course assignments, each referencing one ordinary Course by `course_id`;
- multiple Student-owned Learning Paths with one selected context, item progress, and immutable revisions; only Learning Planner may replace planned routes through its dedicated token;
- read-only legacy student practice-task projects, milestones, artifacts, reviews, and immutable sanitized portfolio publications; writers exist only behind an emergency compatibility flag.
- the idempotent integration inbox and curated teacher assistance evidence associated with opaque learning targets.
- distinct student-owned learning-action cycles, their frozen ordered target snapshots, and the durable closure outbox.
- immutable normalized action-target evidence, the policy-versioned target mastery projection, and reducer audit history.
- trusted Course task metadata, including ordered opaque learning-target references used by later student-owned evidence production.
- the safe read projection of a student-owned learning action used by task-scoped teacher context construction.
- the bounded learner overview used by general PersonalTeacher dialogs.
- the strict read-only planning-readiness snapshot, derived from accepted draft/profile facts and the exact selected active path; Planner owns all planning decisions.
- immutable Planner-fixed official diagnostic assessment attempts, frozen task references, submissions, receipts, and placement-only results (migration 028); reservation uses the dedicated Course diagnostic catalogue capability and deterministic idempotent replay.

It consumes but does not own:

- course, lesson, task, position, assessment definition, and completion metadata from `ms-go-course`;
- v2 practice task instances, execution, review, and results from `ms-go-practice-task-orchestrator`; Practice emits the resulting exact target evidence to Student;
- workspace, snapshot, preview, live validation, and archive operations from `ms-go-sandbox`;
- authenticated stage-based final validation from `ms-go-validation-orchestrator`;
- file blobs represented by stored file IDs from `ms-go-filestorage`.
- teacher-owned assistance facts from `ms-go-teacher-agent`.
- Course assignment and route-replacement commands from `ms-go-learning-planner`; Student remains authoritative for assignment/path state, item progress, evidence, and mastery.

## Learning evidence boundary

Practice submits `practice-task-competency-evidence.v1` only after a passed
result. The bundle carries exact versioned targets, correctness, independence,
confidence, Step attribution, and assistance summary. Student validates identity
and idempotency, stores immutable receipt/target rows, maps assistance to
independent/guided evidence, runs the same `student-mastery-v1` reducer used by
learning actions, and stores a separate audit in one transaction. Student never
reinterprets the Practice task result and Practice never writes mastery.

An answer and a learning action are different identities. One answer may own several ordered action cycles when activity reopens a failed or rejected answer. The action snapshots task targets when it opens. Terminal closure stores the answer update, action `closed_at`, and `learning_action.closed` outbox envelope in one transaction; the relay publishes it at least once to `TASKANSWER_EVENTS`.

`teacher.assistance.observed` is consumed from the durable `TEACHER_EVENTS` stream. A valid envelope represents exactly one learning action and contains `observations[]` over opaque `{type, key, optional version}` targets. The inbox marker, action assistance summary, and target observations commit in one PostgreSQL transaction before explicit acknowledgement. Redelivery of the same `event_id` is a no-op.

Teacher facts can record independent/guided context, hints, and interventions. They cannot assert task success, score, confidence, or mastery and do not update mastery directly. Student freezes the task evidence class when the action opens and stores the official outcome when it closes. Only after exact assistance correlation does the deterministic `student-mastery-v1` reducer create normalized action-target evidence, the current target projection, and an audit record. See [Objective evidence and mastery policy v1](objective-mastery.md).

Teacher-agent may read one action through the internal ownership-scoped context endpoint. The response contains action/task/context identity, the immutable target snapshot, `OPEN|CLOSED`, and `opened_at`; it never exposes answer identity, objective outcome, evidence class, raw evidence, or audit. Teacher then queries mastery only for those exact targets and constructs its bounded request context in memory.

## Core rule

Official diagnostics are a separate placement-only aggregate. They do not
create ordinary answers, learning actions, evidence, mastery, progression,
paths, or events; receipt replay is resolved before external Course catalogue
or task-definition reads. See [Official diagnostic assessments](diagnostic-assessments.md).

Live validation is Sandbox feedback and never grants an ordinary Course attempt `PASSED`. Student owns that status; Practice owns v2 practice submission/result status.

The remaining milestone/runtime/final-review implementation below is compatibility v1 only. Default routing prevents all new mutation and returns `410 Gone`; `LEGACY_PRACTICE_RUNTIME_WRITES_ENABLED=true` is an explicit temporary rollback switch. Historical rows without a revision ID retain their prior live-context compatibility read behavior.

Legacy handlers/tables can be deleted only after usage APIs report no retained
catalog references, portfolio/history consumers are migrated, rollback support
is closed, and the emergency flag has remained unused for the agreed retention
window. Until then they are isolated compatibility data, not a competing owner.

Authored revisions also carry each milestone's student-safe starter workspace and runtime profile. These values take precedence over local starter builders and milestone-kind runtime switches, which remain only for legacy snapshots where the fields are absent. Authored paths are checked again before sandbox materialization and malformed stored data fails closed. Private test-suite, reference-solution, negative-fixture, and verifier references are not part of the runtime-context contract.

The selected solution variant also owns an immutable final-review policy. After all deterministic milestones pass, a version-1 policy moves the project to `READY_FOR_REVIEW`. Submission obtains the current sandbox snapshot and re-runs every milestone selected by the pinned variant through `ms-go-validation-orchestrator` in final mode. Only a complete deterministic pass can create a review. The service then optionally runs schema-validated AI review and always waits for a mentor decision. The AI prompt contract, mentor rubric, and opaque authoring-test references are read from the pinned revision's private evaluation context; only the public policy is present in normal runtime context. AI output is advisory and cannot finalize the project.

Variant milestones may carry explicit ordered lesson bindings with project-step instructions. These bindings replace skill-tag inference for that milestone. Required lessons block milestone execution; recommended and optional lessons are shown without blocking. Completing any required lesson in an `alternative_group` satisfies that one-of unit. A `prerequisite_group` is one route stage: lessons within it can be opened in any order, while incomplete required units in earlier stages block later lessons. Completion remains student-global, so the same lesson is immediately recognized in another variant or practice task.

After mentor approval, the owner may create one portfolio publication for the completed runtime. Its source is the exact immutable artifact referenced by the passed review, not the mutable sandbox. The service creates a deterministic text-only sanitized snapshot, stores its checksum and frozen task/result metadata, encrypts the snapshot before FileStorage upload, and controls `private`, `unlisted`, and `public` visibility in PostgreSQL. Public endpoints return source text for a read-only code viewer only; they never expose or control live runtime infrastructure. See [Practice-task portfolio publication](practice-task-publication.md).

See [Security and consistency limits](security-and-consistency.md) before changing authentication, events, or multi-step writes.

## Accepted Hybrid Replanning business architecture (Problem #4)

The authoritative [Hybrid Mastery → Replanning decision](https://github.com/bemulima/ms-go-learning-planner/blob/main/docs/hybrid-mastery-replanning.md) separates Evidence
and Mastery updates from Planner evaluation and actual Path mutation. Student owns
authoritative learner/Mastery snapshots, evaluation initiation, consent and
preferences, safe-boundary and expected-revision validation, atomic Path revision
application, idempotency, and applied-decision provenance. Planner alone decides
`NO_CHANGE` / `REPLAN_NEEDED` and supplies the desired mutation.

Completed history is immutable; ACTIVE work and existing Practice TaskInstances
are protected. Ordinary mutation affects PENDING work after current-item completion
and before next-item activation. Exceptional interruption requires explicit student
intent and an available Runtime-confirmed safe checkpoint/hold/resume capability.
Pause/resume is optional: without it, ACTIVE Practice is not interrupted for
remediation, which waits for the ordinary boundary. Activity/Revision owners
confirm INVALID; Runtime owners confirm IMPOSSIBLE. Planner decides the planning
consequence and Student applies authoritative learner/Path state. This is an
accepted business architecture, not a change to current wire contracts or the
completion reducer. See [the local boundary](learning-paths-and-context.md#accepted-hybrid-replanning-boundary-problem-4).
